scope: Independent read-only peer review of hosted public guest Chat run 37748038743; no native rerun or source fix.

verdict_a_observed_behavior.opening: PASS: the signed-out guest sent a new conversation, received HTTP 200, and reached a terminal assistant answer containing the unpredictable opening code and ordered page stages.
verdict_a_observed_behavior.same_conversation_followup: PASS: is_new=false with the opening conversation fingerprint; HTTP 200 and a separate terminal reply contained the follow-up code and fixture heading.
verdict_a_observed_behavior.post_reload_new_conversation: FAIL: a new panel document and distinct is_new=true conversation were observed. The initial Chat POST returned HTTP 200; get_page_text completed with the fixture URL, opening code, follow-up code, and heading. The continuation stream then emitted HTTP 409 with no classified code. After the driver's 180-second bound, the panel had zero assistant replies and no terminal answer.
verdict_a_observed_behavior.failure_boundary: Between successful delegated get_page_text completion and a terminal assistant reply from the resumed stream. The continuation response body, backend request state, and exact 409 cause were not captured; assigning a server-only or client-only root cause would exceed this evidence.
verdict_a_observed_behavior.classification: Observed product-path failure on this published artifact/server pair, not a mere missing fixture or resource rejection. Harness influence and recurrence are not ruled out by one run.

verdict_b_evidence_quality.run_provenance: GitHub run 37748038743 is completed/failure at head 3ab075f80468a407bb44b246771289a98d75d086; local driver hash matches that checkout. The original receipt and three journals match the hashes recorded in the primary report.
verdict_b_evidence_quality.artifact_and_server: Receipt identifies public Store CRX 0.2.205, adapted and unpacked, tree SHA-256 08967843dbbd065a2fdfea1a17f4c61aca1c8a251ab0bc720ee825ec6a6fd8b8. Health/version before and after the run, plus this peer spot-check, show server SHA 53aec906f047b524495ff0d93bae8e67eb55537f.
verdict_b_evidence_quality.resources: Package and browser jobs exited zero with valid resource decisions. Guest was admitted, watched as healthy throughout, then exited one with resourceInvalid=false and decision=child_failed. Resource pressure does not explain the observed assertion failure.
verdict_b_evidence_quality.oracle_and_driver: The driver installs a stream collector before each send, verifies an actual new panel document after reload, checks fixture readability and active tab, and calls the same composer send UI. Its terminal oracle requires a rendered assistant answer beyond the prior reply count; the post-reload failure screenshot independently shows the question and extracted-text tool row without a reply.
verdict_b_evidence_quality.comparison: Run 37649504416 passed all three turns with the same Store artifact tree on server 8fe201b44e7a4c8fe3bf726b77546ad533926a60. This is a useful working sibling, but the two hosted runs do not isolate a server change because timing, state, and execution also differ.
limits: The CRX was adapted and loaded unpacked; installation through Chrome Web Store UI was not tested.
The CDP observer attached after panel load. It recorded the three initial Chat POSTs, not the continuation HTTP exchange; the latter status comes from the panel stream trace.
The stream trace has HTTP 409 with code=null. That is not evidence for a specific protocol reason such as resume_conflict or outstanding_delegated_calls.
One failed run proves the bounded failure, not its frequency or root cause. No native rerun was performed in this independent review.

next_diagnostic_evidence: At the failed turn, correlate the guest Chat conversation fingerprint, user_request/run identifiers, delegated get_page_text call, posted tool result, and the /resume request on both client and server. Record only safe structured metadata, not secrets or page text.

Capture the continuation endpoint, response status and structured refusal code, server request snapshot/trace, and whether the tool result was accepted before resume; identify the first boundary where the expected continuation ceased.
Run one pinned reproduction on the same CRX/server pair with that capture, then vary only the server SHA or a single continuation condition against the passing sibling.
